capitals.name: Sapa / Namayan (Santa Ana, Manila)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital: Namayan, Mandaluyong or Sapa'; the Santa Ana page equates Sapa with the Santa Ana district of Manila. The pages give no coordinates; the dot is the district's approximate position (the gazetteer has no Santa Ana of Manila), and the page names three candidate sites, so it is a placeholder.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria begins Namayan in 1202, but the infobox gives 'Established: before the 11th century' and the page says it 'is believed to have peaked in the 11th-14th centuries'; the History of the Philippines (900-1565) table agrees ('Before the 11th century - 1571'). 1000 is the latest year that fits 'before the 11th century'; the shape is Cliopatria's 1202 shape plus the districts of the Santa Ana page. No area on either page.

The grid cells are about 253 km2 each, so the added Mandaluyong, Makati and Pasay land is two cells that Cliopatria's Maynila (c. 1500 onward) and Tondo shapes also touch, a contest no page describes. The page dates no extent.

ledger.note: By 1000: Namayan already exists on the Pasig River's upper reaches. Infobox 'Established: before the 11th century' and 'Formed as a polity occupying several barangays'; no founding year or founder is given (the original residents trace their origin to 'a ruler ("regulo") called Lacantagcan'), so 1000 is the latest year consistent with the page and Cliopatria's 1202 is not on it.

ledger.note: 1571: Namayan passes to Spain. Infobox 'Conquest by Spain: 1571'. The page describes no fighting at Namayan; the Maynila page has Legazpi's forces arrive and Manila declared a Spanish city on 24 June 1571, and the Santa Ana page has the Franciscans receive the land (Santa Ana de Sapa, 1578). The land named is read from the Santa Ana page.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of the Pasig River polities
wars.outcome: Spain took Maynila (battle of 1570, Legazpi's arrival and the founding of Manila on 24 June 1571) and Tondo (the last resistance on 3 June 1571); the Namayan page records only 'Conquest by Spain: 1571'.
wars.note: 'This "Battle of Maynila" ended with a fire that destroyed the fortified settlement of Maynila'; 'Maynila was declared as the new Spanish city of Manila on June 24, 1571'. Neither the Maynila nor the Tondo page describes any action at Namayan, so no zone is set.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary: the extent is a list of modern districts, and the grid cells are larger than the polity.

notes: Page budget up to 5 pages, all used; the five pages together give no founding year, no territorial change and no vassal tie for Namayan. Start year 1000 is the latest year that fits 'Established: before the 11th century' (Namayan page and the History of the Philippines table), at confidence 1; Cliopatria's 1202 is on neither page. The Cliopatria outline (4 to 6 grid cells, about 1,000 km2) lies south-east of the core the Santa Ana page describes, so every shape is adjusted by adding Mandaluyong, Makati and Pasay; the three districts share cells with Cliopatria's Maynila and Tondo shapes (a contest on the grid, not a dated one). The cell losses of 1375 and 1497 are not explained by any page. Legends on the pages are not territory: a 'lady of Namayan' marrying 'Emperor Soledan' at the Majapahit court, and Pasay's mother of 'Bornean lineage'; no page makes Namayan a vassal or tributary of Majapahit, Brunei, Tondo or Maynila. Not settled: the extent in the early 1570s (Rajah Kalamayin's domain), the capital's coordinates (Namayan, Mandaluyong or Sapa), the barangays of the confederation beyond the five the Namayan page names (Namayan, Sapa, Meycatmon, Dilao, Meysapan). No new gazetteer names needed (Pandacan and Paco lie inside the City of Manila admin-1 and are not added separately).
